challenge.better_approach: Changing the proxies' device_id to their folder names would also do it, but it reds dbproxy's own falsifier ('when the shim's device_id or the charter's answers_as is not database') and the bus name; keying the file by folder in the base shim is the smaller change and matches bin/cairn's rule.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That only last_known is written under the alias dir: measured, ~/.cairn/devices/database/0 and inference/0 hold only last_known.json. And that folder_of reading charters per persist is cheap: rack iterates ~20 folders, cached on the shim.
challenge.prior_art: CairnCommons/tickets/8c5fdb750b75-a-charter-s-answers-as-outranks-a-stray-instance-space-dir-of-that-name.json fixed the launcher side and named this as its own ticket; bin/cairn's answers_as block and cairn/tools/rack/rack.py folder_of already resolve alias to folder; grep of tickets/ and questions/ for _last_known_path found no ticket for it.
challenge.real_collision: None exclusive: 8c5fdb750b75 rules a declared name outranks a stray dir, which this removes rather than contradicts; device_id stays the bus name.

answers.falsifier: a shim whose device_id is a charter's answers_as persists last_known at instance_path(<declaring folder>, n)/last_known.json, and nothing is created at instance_path(device_id, n); a shim whose device_id is no charter's answers_as persists last_known at instance_path(device_id, n)/last_known.json, byte-path unchanged; migration: with last_known only at the old alias address, a fresh shim's cold read returns that record, the record then stands under the folder, and the alias file, its <n>/ dir and the alias dir are gone; with a record at both addresses, the cold read returns the folder's and the alias file is gone; no other caller of the last_known path breaks: cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_shim.py, test_root_verbs.py, test_root_verb_vocabulary.py and bin/proofs/test_a_declared_name_outranks_a_stray_instance_dir.py pass unchanged
answers.from_idea: none, because the debt was named in CairnCommons/tickets/8c5fdb750b75-a-charter-s-answers-as-outranks-a-stray-instance-space-dir-of-that-name.json bounds.out, not captured as an idea
answers.how: BaseShim._last_known_path keys by the folder rack.folder_of(device_id) names when device_id is a charter's answers_as, else by device_id unchanged (the launcher's own rule, bin/cairn answers_as block). _read_last_known migrates: when the folder record is absent and the alias record stands, it reads the alias record, writes it under the folder atomically, removes the alias file and then the alias <n>/ and <alias>/ dirs if left empty; when both stand, it reads the folder record and removes the alias one. The red-first proof runs over a scratch instance root (address.ROOTS) with a throwaway shim whose device_id is a real charter's answers_as.
answers.traces_to: Law 5 (the address carries what a mind needs now: an alias dir holding a stray cache misstates what devices exist) and Law 6 (one owner: the dbproxy record berths under dbproxy's address, not a second one)
answers.what: A shim keeps its last_known under the rack folder that declares it, so a device whose shim answers to a declared name (dbproxy as database, inferenceproxy as inference) writes no alias-named directory in instance-space, and the strays already standing migrate home once and are gone.

bullets.text: Two live alias dirs (database/0, inference/0) exist only because BaseShim keys last_known by device_id; this ticket migrates them home.
